AXP.rationale: AXP presents a solid fundamental case with accelerating revenue (+8.6% YoY to $11.21B), expanding operating margins (36.3%), and strong cash generation (OCF $5.37B, +23.1% YoY). The integrated issuer-network model provides structural revenue diversification, and pricing power was validated by the Platinum Card fee increase to $895 with 15% fee revenue growth. Credit quality remains pristine at 2.0% net write-offs. The most compelling signal is valuation: trailing P/E of 20x sits near the floor of its 18.4x-25.3x range despite ROE improving to 33.4% and EPS growing 11% YoY — a clear disconnect between fundamentals and market pricing. However, several factors temper conviction: (1) the Q2 expense surge (+12% to $14.5B) outpacing revenue growth signals near-term margin uncertainty from reinvestment, (2) balance-sheet leverage at ~8x liabilities-to-equity amplifies downside in credit-stress scenarios, (3) the AML enforcement overhang (Law360, 2026-07-27) has uncertain magnitude, and (4) analyst fair-value ranges cluster $280-$379, placing the stock near the upper end. The Q2 earnings beat (EPS $4.53 vs $4.40 consensus) and raised full-year revenue guidance to 10% provide a modest near-term catalyst, but the post-earnings selloff of ~6.5% suggests the market is already digesting the expense concern. On balance, the fundamental trajectory is positive and valuation is attractive vs. own history, but leverage, regulatory risk, and the expense-growth question prevent a higher conviction score.
key_factors: Revenue growth accelerating: +8.6% YoY to $11.21B in Q2 2026, with full-year guidance raised to 10% revenue growth
Operating margin expanding to 36.3% (Q2 2026), up from 34.4% year-ago, with mid-36% becoming the new run-rate
EPS diluted growing +11% YoY to $4.53, outpacing revenue growth and indicating positive operating leverage
Operating cash flow robust at $5.37B (+23.1% YoY), covering net income by 1.73x
P/E of 20x near floor of 18.4x-25.3x range despite accelerating earnings — valuation compressed vs own history
ROE improved to 33.4% from 31.4% year-ago while P/B compressed to 6.69x (near floor of 6.1x-8.2x range)
Pricing power validated: Platinum Card fee increase to $895 drove 15% YoY fee revenue growth with strong acceptance
Credit quality pristine: net write-off rates at 2.0% flat YoY, provisions for credit losses down from $1.4B to $1.1B
Millennial/Gen Z represent 65% of new accounts, supporting long-term cardmember base growth
Balance-sheet leverage at ~8x liabilities-to-equity ($273.92B liabilities / $34.28B equity) amplifies downside in credit-stress scenarios
Q2 consolidated expenses rose 12% to $14.5B, outpacing revenue growth and spooking investors — stock fell ~6.5% on earnings day
AML enforcement risk: Law360 (2026-07-27) reported AXP may face regulatory fines over AML compliance deficiencies
Earnings yield of 5.0% barely clears 10-year Treasury yield of 4.68%, limiting valuation safety net if rates rise
Analyst fair-value estimates cluster $280-$379, with stock at ~$337 near upper end of range

fee revenue grew 15% year-over-year, driven by strong customer acceptance of the Platinum Card's $200 annual fee increase to $895... Millennials/Gen Z represent 65% of new accounts.

American Express Co. may face regulatory fines over its anti-money-laundering compliance programs and has been working to 'identify and remediate deficiencies' in them.

American Express released its 2026 DFAST results, confirming a 2.5% Stress Capital Buffer through September 30, 2027. The company returned $8.7 billion to shareholders... raised its quarterly dividend by 16% to $0.95 per share.

With average import tariffs in the U.S. reaching 13%, this could erode purchasing power, even among Amex's affluent customer base... the CFPB continues to push for lower late fees and interest rate caps.
Despite having fewer users, American Express consistently earns more in revenue than Mastercard and Visa combined.
